Running command: cat > /workspace/candidate_trace.json << 'EOF'
[
  {"step": 1, "file": "tests/oss-fuzz/rules_fuzzer.cc", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 28, "var": "buffer", "code": "yr_compiler_add_string(compiler, (const char*) buffer, NULL)", "note": "Attacker-controlled YARA rule source code enters the compiler"},
  {"step": 2, "file": "libyara/grammar.y", "function": "string_declaration", "line": 574, "var": "$3 (hex string)", "code": "yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration(yyscanner, STRING_GFLAGS_HEXADECIMAL, $1, $3, &$$)", "note": "Hex string rule is parsed and reduced"},
  {"step": 3, "file": "libyara/parser.c", "function": "yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration", "line": 542, "var": "re_ast", "code": "result = yr_re_parse_hex(str->c_string, &re_ast, &re_error)", "note": "Hex string '{ 61 [201] }' is parsed into RE_AST with CONCAT root containing LITERAL(61) and RANGE_ANY(201)"},
  {"step": 4, "file": "libyara/parser.c", "function": "yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration", "line": 604, "var": "re_ast, remainder_re_ast", "code": "result = yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point(re_ast, &re_ast, &remainder_re_ast, &min_gap, &max_gap)", "note": "Split at RANGE_ANY(201) which is at end of children list"},
  {"step": 5, "file": "libyara/re.c", "function": "yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point", "line": 498, "var": "re_ast->root_node->children_head", "code": "re_ast->root_node->children_head = child->next_sibling;", "note": "children_head updated to NULL but children_tail NOT updated, still points to RANGE_ANY(201)"},
  {"step": 6, "file": "libyara/re.c", "function": "yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point", "line": 514, "var": "child (RANGE_ANY)", "code": "yr_re_node_destroy(child);", "note": "RANGE_ANY(201) node is freed, but re_ast->root_node->children_tail still points to it"},
  {"step": 7, "file": "libyara/parser.c", "function": "_yr_parser_write_string", "line": 335, "var": "literal_string", "code": "literal_string = yr_re_ast_extract_literal(re_ast);", "note": "Called with re_ast whose children_tail is a dangling pointer"},
  {"step": 8, "file": "libyara/re.c", "function": "yr_re_ast_extract_literal", "line": 367, "var": "child", "code": "child = re_ast->root_node->children_tail;", "note": "Reads freed RANGE_ANY node from children_tail"},
  {"step": 9, "file": "libyara/re.c", "function": "yr_re_ast_extract_literal", "line": 369, "var": "child->type", "code": "while (child != NULL && child->type == RE_NODE_LITERAL)", "note": "READ 4 from freed heap memory at child->type — use-after-free crash"}
]
EOF

message.content:
Now let me create the candidate trace JSON. Based on my analysis:

1. The attacker-controlled input is the YARA rule source code
2. It flows through `yr_compiler_add_string` -> parser -> `yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration`
3. The hex string `{ 61 [201] }` is parsed into a RE_AST with CONCAT root containing LITERAL(61) and RANGE_ANY(201)
4. `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point` splits at RANGE_ANY(201), but fails to update `children_tail`
5. `yr_re_ast_extract_literal` reads from the freed `children_tail` pointer (use-after-free)
